**What.** Every smoke test passes when it runs alone, and the README's prose keeps within 120 columns.

## Part 29: what the review found (planned 2026-10-13)

The owner's twenty-eighth word, on 2026-10-13, while part 28 closed: start a review as well, and do everything the
project still lacks.

**Status (2026-10-13): planned.** Four reviewers read the code by area, without running anything: the agent's core and
the store; the tools; the models, the policy, the configuration and the command line; the server, the pages, the desktop
shell and the docs. Each was given the same five criteria: a contract the code breaks (its docstring, the README, an
as-built text here), a failure hidden or put down to the wrong cause, a secret or the owner's data that can leak or a
check that an ordinary path skips, the owner's goals (going on after a break, a closed app or a restart; using what the
system offers), and a capability the README describes that the code lacks. They reported 38 findings. Each was read
again in the code before it became an item, and so were five that part 28's report had left open. Two findings were not
borne out: a write of a campaign outside the store's write lock (every method that writes holds it, which a scan of the
store confirmed) and MCP servers outliving the hub (the MCP library ends a server's whole process group).

**The shape of this part (the decisions).** Seven items, each a pull request of its own, the most important first:
protected files stay out of `web_extract`, a file of the workspace is read as one, and the README names none of the
owner's own skills (174); one broken MCP server never keeps Dot from starting (175); long skills and PDFs are read in
pages, and `osascript` ends with its run (176); the configuration refuses at load what would fail a run (177); the
server answers every failure as JSON, and a page says when it could not read again (178); a run's end is one write, and
a chat a run works on is never deleted (179); a campaign whose session's command died goes on (180). Not in this part,
each for a reason: a run of a `dotx` command shown live on the pages (the owner has not run one; a feature of its own);
a send whose answer was lost, checked with the daemon before it is sent again (the API, the pages and the store
together); the doctor's check of OpenAI and OpenCode Go model names against the lists they serve; a 403 that is not
about the key; a queued message removed in the moment it starts; a journal line cut short by a full disk; the errors of
the desktop shell's own reads; the shape of a failed run's result (the owner's rule keeps a request and its answer in an
error's context). Two decisions are the owner's: whether installing a package asks once the run has read what a third
party wrote, and whether an MCP server's own word that a tool only reads is trusted (it is, and item 175 has the README
say so).

### How to start part 29 (the handoff prompt)

> Read ROADMAP.md part 29 and the status table of part 9 (rows 174 to 180). One item at a time, in order; the protocol
> of part 5 (branch, gate, PR, Linear MYP issue when the connector is signed in, squash merge, hash in the table, log
> line) is unchanged. Read each finding again in the code before closing it, give each change a test that fails on the
> code of before, and check a page that changes in a browser, wide and on a phone, light and dark. Never touch the
> owner's data directory except to read it, by the kinds and numbers of what is stored, and to restart the daemon when
> `/api/status` shows no active run; PLAN.md stays untracked. The owner reads Turkish; everything written is English.

### 174. Protected files stay out of web_extract, and a workspace file is read as one

**Status: done.** Merged as `3f450ef` (PR #212; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-13).** `web_extract` reads a file only after the check `read_file` makes. A file's text goes to the
fast model, so a source in a protected location gives the call the `secret_access` flag (`read_flags`, which the file
tools share), and the review that is always on refuses it outside a `yolo` run. A source is a file when the workspace
has a file by that name, even one whose name looks like an address (`notes.md`), or when it is a path; before, a name
with no slash before its first dot was fetched from the web (`https://notes.md`). Files are resolved as the file tools
resolve them. The README names none of the owner's own skills: two of them were named as examples in the README and in
two entries of this file since 2026-10-09, and a unit test used one of the names. The README also names `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`
among the variables the shell tool leaves out, with `[shell] pass_env` to keep it. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_crawl.py`
reads a file of the workspace whose name looks like a host, with a web client that fails the test when anything is
fetched (the code of before fetched `https://prices-174.md`), and names a protected file to `web_extract`, which gets
the flag `read_file` gets and is refused by the review (the code of before gave it no flag).

**What.** `web_extract` refuses a file in a protected location, as `read_file` does, since the file's text goes to the
fast model; a file of the workspace is read by its name even when the name looks like an address; the README names none
of the owner's own skills.

### 175. One broken MCP server never keeps Dot from starting

**Status: done.** Merged as `637e979` (PR #213; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-13).** An MCP server is checked when it starts: each tool it offers, after `allow` and `deny`, has
an input schema Dot can hand to a model (`tool_parameters`, which the registration of the tools uses too). A tool whose
schema has a reference that leads nowhere, or nests deeper than Dot follows, leaves its server out with the reason, the
server and the tool named and the hint to leave the tool out with `allow`, as a server that cannot start is left out;
before, the server came up, the registration of its tools failed, and Dot did not start. `dotx mcp list` reports any
failure of a server as the hub does, one that is not Dot's own with its type, and goes on to the next server; before,
such a failure ended the command. A server whose working directory is missing is reported as such, with the directory,
rather than as a command that was not found. The README names these reasons among those a server is left out for, and
says that a server's own word that a tool only reads is trusted. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_mcp.py` starts a server whose
tool takes a tree (a node that holds nodes) next to a good one: the tree's server is left out with the reason and the
good one serves (the code of before connected both); the report of `dotx mcp list` goes on past a fault of the MCP
library (the code of before let it out); a missing working directory is named (the code of before said the command was
not found).

**What.** An MCP server whose tool has an input schema Dot cannot use is left out with the reason when it starts, as a
server that cannot start is, instead of keeping Dot from starting; `dotx mcp list` reports every failure of a server
instead of stopping at the first that is not one of Dot's own; a working directory that is missing is named as such
rather than as a missing command; the README says that a server's own word that a tool only reads is trusted.

### 176. Long skills and PDFs are read in pages, and osascript ends with its run

**Status: done.** Merged as `15286a3` (PR #214; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-13).** The `skill` tool hands a skill's instructions over in parts when they are longer than one
tool result: each part fits the result next to the first line, the fence and, in the first part only, the list of the
skill's files (at most a quarter of the result, the rest counted), and a part that does not reach the end says where the
next one starts (`skill(name=…, start=…)`). A part ends at a line or word break, as a window of `web_fetch` does
(`text_window`, which the two share now), and holds at least 1,000 characters however little room the rest leaves; a
start past the end is refused with the length of the instructions. Before, the whole of a long skill went into one
result, and the cut every result gets took its middle. `read_file` pages the text of a PDF by its lines with `offset`
and `limit`, as it pages a text file, each page ending with the line to go on from; before, it ignored both and cut the
middle out of a long PDF. `osascript` is killed when its call is cancelled, by a stopped run or by the tool's own
timeout, as a cancelled search is; before, a script that waited went on without its run. The browser's driver stops when
Dot lets go of Chrome even if the close of Chrome fails with an error that is not Playwright's; before, the driver
stayed running, and so did the Chrome it started, holding the profile. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_skills_runtime.py` reads
a skill six times as long as a result in parts, each within the result, that join to the whole instructions, the files
in the first part only (the code of before gave one result of 74,965 characters); `tests/unit/test_read_pdf.py` reads
lines 21 to 30 of a PDF of 60 lines (the code of before began at line 1); `tests/unit/test_osascript_cancel.py` cancels
a script that waits and finds no `osascript` left (the code of before left it running);
`tests/smoke/test_browser_profile.py` makes the close of Dot's own Chrome fail and finds the profile free within seconds
(the code of before left a Chrome holding it).

**What.** The `skill` tool gives a long skill's instructions in parts with the place to go on from, and `read_file`
pages a PDF's text as it pages a text file, instead of cutting out their middle; an `osascript` whose run is stopped or
whose tool times out is killed; the browser's driver stops even when Chrome's close fails.

### 177. The configuration refuses at load what would fail a run

**Status: done.** Merged as `ce5b468` (PR #215; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-13).** The configuration is refused when it loads, with the key named, for what would fail every run
later. An address of a provider or of the judge has to be `http://` or `https://` with a host, read as the HTTP client
reads it (`ServiceAddress`); before, a malformed one failed every call of the provider with an error of the client. A
model has to be `<provider>:<model>` with a provider Dot knows (`ModelReference`, by `split_model_ref`, the one rule
`parse_model_ref` uses as well), and `[models] search` an Anthropic model. A site under `[policy.spend]` has to be a
bare host in lower case without `www.` (`SpendSite`), the form a payment step's address is matched in; a cap under
another name never applied. The budgets and timeouts that no run can work with are refused: a tool output under 2,000
characters (the floor a run keeps however small its window), a context budget of 0 or less, a shell timeout under 1
second or a default above `max_timeout_s`, and a timeout of 0 or less for the login shell's environment, the desktop's
reads, captures, launches and scripts, and a fetch. A budget above 0 that the system prompt and the tools fill is still
refused when a run starts, where the model is known (`require_room`). A Keychain that does not answer within 15 seconds
is a `ConfigError` that names the key and says what to do, instead of the timeout of a child process. `dotx models` ends
with 1 when no provider answered; before, only when the one provider it was given failed. The comment on
`[agent] resume` names the runs of a `dotx` command that can be resumed (a closed terminal, SIGTERM, a command that
died) and says that Ctrl-C is a stop. The owner's configuration was loaded under the new checks before the merge, and
passes. Tests: `tests/unit/test_config_bounds.py` refuses each of these values with its key;
`tests/unit/test_keychain_timeout.py` finds that error for a Keychain that times out; `tests/smoke/test_cli_models.py`
runs `dotx models` in a child process with every provider at a closed port and the keys in its environment, so the
Keychain is never read, and it ends with 1. Each failed on the code of before.

**What.** The configuration is refused when it loads, with the key named, for what would fail every run later: a
provider's address that is not an `http://` or `https://` address with a host, a context or a timeout of zero, a model
that names no known provider, a spending cap whose site is not a bare host. A Keychain that does not answer is a Dot
error that says so; `dotx models` ends with 1 when every provider failed; the comment on `resume` names the `dotx`
commands.

### 178. The server answers every failure as JSON, and a page says it could not read again

**Status: done.** Merged as `401cef2` (PR #216; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-13).** Every error of the API comes as `{"message": …, "context": {…}}`: those of the web framework
itself (a path that does not exist, a method a path does not take) with their status and headers, and an error that is
not one of Dot's own as a 500 whose context names its kind and its words (secrets redacted, cut to 500 characters),
logged as `request_crashed` with its traceback. Before, such an error came as the plain text "Internal Server Error" and
Dot's log did not have it. The sign-in page tells a daemon that answered with an error from one that does not answer: it
says that the daemon runs, shows the error and where the log is, instead of asking to start the daemon. A page that
cannot read again what it shows, after an event of the stream or once the stream is back, keeps what it showed and says
so in a toast while the stream is live (`readFailed`, told at most every ten seconds together with the events a page
could not show), as item 160 meant; before, the activity, the schedules, a run's page, the sidebar, the queue and the
home wrote it to the console only. A page whose read fails later, not at once, is told too, since the pages' re-readers
are followed to their end. The lifecycle stream tells a page whose events were lost because it fell behind to read
everything again (`resync`), as a break of the stream does; before, the page never knew. The README says that a phone's
push comes while one looks at its run on the phone too, as it always did. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_server.py` makes the
themes folder unreadable and gets a 500 in the shape of every error, with the kind of the error, and the log entry; a
path that does not exist is a 404 in that shape (the code of before answered the plain text);
`tests/unit/test_events.py` floods the lifecycle stream and is told to read again (the code of before was not);
`tests/smoke/test_page_guards.py` signs in to a daemon that answers an error (the code of before asked to start it) and
makes the home's read fail after an event: the home keeps what it showed and a toast says so (the code of before said
nothing). The pages were looked at in a browser, wide and on a phone, light and dark.

**What.** Every error of the API comes as `{"message": …, "context": {…}}` and an error that is not one of Dot's own is
logged with its traceback; sign-in says what failed when the daemon answered; a page that could not read again after the
stream came back says so, as item 160 meant; a stream that fell behind tells the page to read again.

### 179. A run's end is one write, and a chat a run works on is never deleted

**Status: done.** Merged as `be314c3` (PR #217; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-13).** The end of a run that started is one write: `Store.end_run` stores the run's status and
result, the scores of the notes it was handed and its `run_finished` event in one transaction that holds the write lock
from its start, and returns the event, which the manager hands to the listeners (`EventBus.publish`). Before, they were
three writes, and a status could be stored with its event lost: a page or a `dotx` command following the run waited for
an end the store had. A store that refuses any part keeps none of it, and the run stays as it was while it worked until
it is closed as a run left behind. A run that could not start is stored as failed, as before. A delegated run whose end
the store could not record is a `StoreError` for the run that delegated it: the call fails and the run goes on; before,
the delegating run read the delegated run as it was while it worked, as its outcome. Deleting chats is refused while a
run of any process works on one of them, itself or through a run it delegated to: the store checks in the transaction of
the deletes, which holds the write lock from its start, and its `RunConflict` (409) names the chats and the runs.
Before, only the daemon's own runs were checked, by the route, and a chat whose run a `dotx` command drove was deleted
under it. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_run_ends.py` makes the database refuse the event of a run's end (a trigger), and the
run's status stays as it was (the code of before stored `done` without the event); a delegated run whose end is refused
that way is an error for the run that delegated it (the code of before returned it as an outcome).
`tests/unit/test_store_writes.py` refuses to delete a chat with a queued run and one whose run delegated to a run that
still works, and deletes it once both are over (the code of before deleted it at once); `tests/smoke/test_server.py`
deletes through the API a chat whose runs only the store has, as a `dotx` command's would be: 409 with the runs, then
200 once they are over (the code of before answered 200 at once).

**What.** A run's end, the close of the notes it used and its `run_finished` event are one write, so a page never waits
for an end that was recorded without its event, and a delegated run whose end was not recorded is an error for the run
that delegated it; deleting a chat is refused while a run of any process works on it, as the README says.

### 180. A campaign whose session's command died goes on

**Status: done.** Merged as `baca51a` (PR #218; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-13).** The daemon plans the next session of a campaign whose session's `dotx` command died when it
closes that session (`close_runs_of_dead_commands`, every half minute while it runs), as after any end of a session:
`campaign_gap_minutes` later, or when the session planned it. Before, the campaign waited for the daemon's next start
(`resume_campaigns`). Such a session is the first one when it came from `dotx run --standing`. A campaign whose opening
session could not start is deleted with the thread made for it, whatever stopped the start (one of Dot's errors, a
fault, a cancelled request), and the deleting is finished through a second cancel. Before, only one of Dot's errors did
it: any other failure kept an active campaign with no session, which the daemon's next start began with no one having
asked again. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_campaigns.py` leaves a session whose owner's lock is gone, as a dead command's is,
and the daemon's check plans the next session the gap later (the code of before planned nothing); it starts a campaign
whose run cannot launch on a full disk, and no campaign and no thread are left, and the daemon's start plans nothing
(the code of before kept the campaign and its thread).

**What.** The next session of a campaign whose session's `dotx` command died is planned when the daemon closes that run,
not at the daemon's next start; a campaign whose start failed in any way is deleted.

## Part 30: the remaining problems (planned 2026-10-13)

The owner's twenty-ninth word, on 2026-10-13, once part 29 was done: do whatever is needed to solve the remaining
problems too.

**Status (2026-10-13): planned.** Three reviewers read again in the code, without running anything, what part 29 left
for later and what its report found: twelve findings it had put off, eight it had found as it went, and the reload of
the desktop app it asked the owner for after an update. Each reviewer was asked whether the code bears a finding out,
with file and line, for the least change that fixes its cause and for a test that fails on the code of before. Twenty
were borne out, three of them in part: a page never sends a message again by itself, so only a second send of a message
whose answer was lost starts it twice; rules change only through the API, so only another window misses a change; the
desktop shell loads its page again after a restart longer than three of its polls, so a quick restart, or a browser tab,
keeps the old scripts. One was not worth an item: the push route takes an endpoint on any https host, but it needs the
token, which already starts any run.

**The shape of this part (the decisions).** Eleven items, each a pull request of its own, the most important first: a
tool that names files works on what was approved, and a journal line cut short is left out (181); a failed run's result
is the error's message, and its context stays in the event (182); a run's end the store refused is stored later, and a
start that failed is told (183); a queued message starts once or is removed, never both (184); a provider's 403 is not a
refused key, and Ollama's stream error keeps its words (185); the doctor checks each model name against the list its
provider serves (186); the service install keeps the running job until the new one is in place (187); a run of a `dotx`
command is followed live on the pages and stopped there (188); a message sent twice starts once (189); the pages say
what they could not read, follow the rules and tell of an update (190); the desktop shell says what it could not read
(191). The owner settled the three questions of part 29's report on 2026-10-13 (open owner decisions 34 to 36): a
package install after a run read what a third party wrote asks no more than before, an MCP server's own word that a tool
only reads is trusted, and the git history keeps the two names item 174 took out of the README.

### 181. Tools that name files work on what was approved, and a cut journal line is left out

**Status: done.** Merged as `05185bc` (PR #220; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-13).** A tool built with `make_path_tool` (`tools/base.py`) is classified again from the files as
they are when it starts, with no wait between that and its run, and refused when that is not the action that was
authorised: a failed call that says what it names changed while it waited, and called again it is decided for where the
path leads now. The file tools (`read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`, `list_dir`, `search_files`, `find_files`),
`web_extract` and `browser_upload` are built so; the shell is not, since its guard reads a command's words, not the
files a program opens (the README calls it best-effort). The undo journal is read as bytes, and what follows its last
line break is left out: a line is written before its change is made, so a line cut short is a change never made. Writing
a line first cuts such a rest off, so that the new line does not run into it. Tests:
`tests/smoke/test_approved_paths.py` moves a link between the authorisation of a `write_file`, and of a `read_file`, and
their run (the code of before wrote, and read, the other file), and `tests/unit/test_undo.py` cuts a line of the journal
short in the middle of a letter, then notes a change and takes the run's changes back (the code of before could not read
the journal any more).

**What.** The tools that name files (the file tools, `web_extract`, `browser_upload`) are classified again as they
start, and a call whose path leads elsewhere by then is refused, instead of reading or writing a file that was not the
one approved; a line of the undo journal that a full disk cut short is left out, instead of failing every later change
of the run and `dotx undo`.

### 182. A failed run's result is the error's message, and its context stays in the event

**Status: done.** Merged as `d1c2a00` (PR #221; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-13).** A run that one of Dot's errors ends stores the error's message as its result
(`RunManager._drive`), which the timeline, the notifications, the push to the phone, `dotx run` and a run that delegated
read; its `run_finished` event keeps the error, its message and its context with the secrets masked (`error`), and the
log keeps the context as before. Before, the result was the error's text with its whole context on the same line
(`message | context={...}`): for a provider's error, the first 3 000 characters of the request and the answer's body, so
the push put the provider's address and the start of the request on the phone's lock screen. A broken connection's
message now says what broke it (`transport failure while talking to the provider (ConnectError: ...)`), which only its
context said, so the result of a run it ends names it too; so does the error of a run that no standby model can take
over, for why the run's model cannot answer and why each standby model was passed over. A tool's failed call still shows
the model the error's context, which tells it what to do next (the nearest lines of an edit that missed, say). Tests:
`tests/smoke/test_model_wait.py` fails a run on a refused request whose error carries a request and an answer, and finds
the message as its result and the error with its context in its `run_finished` event (the code of before stored both on
one line as the result), and `tests/smoke/test_helpers.py` finds why the run's model cannot answer and why its standby
model was passed over in the result of a run that fails so.

**What.** A run that fails on one of Dot's errors stores the error's message as its result, which the pages, the push
and `dotx run` show; the error's context (a provider's request and answer) goes to the `run_finished` event and the log
instead, where it no longer puts the start of a request on the phone's lock screen.

### 183. A run's end the store refused is stored later, and a start that failed is told

**Status: done.** Merged as `265da7c` (PR #222; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-13).** An end of a run that the store refused (a full disk, say) is kept by the run manager and
stored by the daemon's half-minute check (`RunManager.store_left_ends`) once the database takes it, as it was to be
stored: its `run_finished` event is sent to the pages, a campaign's next session is planned and the chat's queue moves
on. Until then a Stop of the run is refused (409) with the reason, and the daemon's next start closes a run whose end is
still left, as before. A run whose start failed after the pages were told it was queued ends through `Store.end_run`, so
its `run_finished` event is stored and sent; before, it was stored failed without one, and a page waited for it. A
cleanup after a failed start (a campaign's opening session, a scheduled run's chat) that fails too is logged, and the
error of the start is the one raised; before, a refused delete replaced it. The run manager's refusal to delete a chat
names its runs (`run_ids`), as the store's does since item 179. A write the database refuses for a reason other than a
lock is a `StoreError` ("the database refused the write", with the method and the database's words), so the half-minute
check logs it and goes on; before, the database's own error ended the check for the daemon's life. Tests:
`tests/smoke/test_run_ends.py` refuses a run's end, then lets the database take it (the code of before left the run at
work until the next start), fails a run's start (no `run_finished` before), fails a campaign's start and its cleanup,
refuses the delete of a chat with a run under way, and refuses the close of a dead command's run under the half-minute
check (it ended before); `tests/unit/test_run_statistics.py` refuses an end and finds no note scored, then stores it and
finds the scores (the code of before raised the database's own error); `tests/unit/test_store_images.py` refuses the
delete of a chat a run works on and finds its screenshots kept.

**What.** An end of a run that the store refused (a full disk) is tried again every half minute until it is stored, with
what follows it, instead of leaving the run at work until the daemon's next start; a run that could not be started
stores its end with its `run_finished` event and tells the pages; a cleanup after a failed start never hides the error
of the start; the manager's refusal to delete a chat names its runs, as the store's does; the half-minute check outlives
a fault of the store; the scores half of item 179's one write and a refused delete that removes no file are tested.

### 184. A queued message starts once or is removed, never both

**Status: done.** Merged as `d462505` (PR #223; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-13).** The first message of a chat's queue is claimed in the store for the chat's next run before
that run starts (`Store.claim_queued`, a row of the new `queue_claims` table, one per chat), in one write, and only when
the queue is not held, no run of any process works on the chat and no message of it is claimed already. The claimed
message leaves the queue once its run has started (`drop_claimed`); when the run could not start, the claim ends, the
message stays first and the queue is held, as before (`hold_claimed`). A claim the store refused to end is ended by the
chat's next start in the process, and a start goes on when the call that began it is cancelled. While it is claimed,
editing it, taking it out or steering it is refused (409, "the message is starting as its chat's next run"), and so is
deleting its chat. A steered message leaves the queue, as it is, before it is sent (`take_queued`); when the run ended
in that moment, the message goes back where it was and the queue moves on as the end of that run does. The claims of a
process that is gone end, at the daemon's start and in its half-minute check, and the queues of their chats are held: a
claimed message whose run that process made leaves the queue, as it started, and any other stays first. Before, a
message left the queue only after its run had started: a removal or an edit in that moment answered success for a
message whose run started anyway, a `dotx` command and the daemon that moved one queue at once could both start its
message, and the daemon started a message beside the run of a `dotx` command at work on the chat. Tests:
`tests/smoke/test_queue.py` removes and edits a message while its run starts (the code of before took both), queues a
message through a second run manager while the first one's run works on the chat (before: it started at once), lets a
held queue go in two run managers at once (before: both started it), holds the queue of a claim whose process is gone,
steers a message as its run ends (it starts after that run) and ends a claim the store refused to end at the chat's next
start; `tests/unit/test_queue_claims.py` covers the claim in the store, two stores on one database and the claim of a
gone process that made its run included.

**What.** A queued message is claimed in the store before its run starts, so a removal, an edit or a steer that comes in
that moment is refused, the message having started, instead of answering success for a message whose run starts anyway;
a `dotx` process that starts the next message of the same chat claims it the same way.

### 185. A provider's 403 is not a refused key, and Ollama's stream error keeps its words

**Status: done.** Merged as `b178796` (PR #224; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-13).** A provider's HTTP 403, as an answer or inside a stream (`permission_error`), is an error of
its own, `ProviderAccessError`, rather than a refused key: the classifier every provider shares (`classify_generic`)
gives 401 to a refused key and 403 to a refused access. A run whose model answers so still moves to its standby model,
with `access refused` as the reason the timeline shows, and the model is paused for `helper_cooldown_s` as before;
Settings › Models says `access refused`, with the provider's words and no link to the keys, which would not help, where
a refused key says `key refused` and links to them. An error Ollama reports inside its stream goes through the table of
stream errors (`error_from_stream`): its message is the provider's words
(`provider answered HTTP 500: model requires more system memory ...`), and its status the one the table gives such an
error, 500 for one it does not name, which is retried as before; before, it was
`provider reported an error inside the stream` under an invented 502, and its words were only in the context. Tests:
`tests/smoke/test_wire_codecs.py` classifies a 403 and a 401, as answers and inside a stream (the code of before called
both a refused key); `tests/unit/test_ollama_finish.py` folds an error chunk of Ollama (before: no words, 502);
`tests/unit/test_helpers.py` pauses a model for a refused access; `tests/smoke/test_provider_problems.py` opens Settings
› Models with providers that refuse access, refuse the key and have none, wide and on a phone, light and dark.

**What.** A provider's HTTP 403 is an error of its own (access refused) rather than a refused key, so the label in
Settings and the reason a run moved to its standby say what the provider said; an error inside Ollama's stream keeps its
words, and its status is the one the table gives such an error instead of an invented 502.

### 186. The doctor checks each model name against the list its provider serves

**Status: done.** Merged as `0b3702a` (PR #225; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-13).** `dotx doctor` reads the list of the models OpenAI and OpenCode Go serve to their keys
(`GET /models`, once for each, within the five seconds of a probe) and checks each configured model of theirs against
it: `main`, `vision`, `fast` and `review`, and each helper and standby model. A model the list leaves out fails
(`openai:gpt-missing: not among the 2 models openai serves to this key (dotx models openai lists them)`), and a helper
or standby model left out is not ready; a list that could not be read makes the model a warning that says why, not a
second failure beside the provider's own row. Ollama and Anthropic answer for the model itself, as before, and a helper
or standby model of theirs is asked too, where only its provider's key was looked at before. The row of OpenAI's key
reads the same list, so OpenAI is asked once. Before, the doctor called every model of OpenAI and OpenCode Go ready
while their keys were set, from what Dot knows of the name alone. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_doctor.py` runs the doctor's
checks of the model services against a stand-in model service on this Mac, through the real connectors: a model OpenAI's
list leaves out fails (the code of before called it ready) and is no ready helper, and a model of OpenCode Go whose list
answers 404 is a warning.

**What.** `dotx doctor` asks the OpenAI and OpenCode Go services for the models their keys may use and fails a
configured model that is not among them, as it does for Ollama and Anthropic, instead of calling every name ready; a
list that cannot be read says so without failing the check twice.

### 187. The service install keeps the running job until the new one is in place

**Status: done.** Merged as `2ad0df4` (PR #226; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-13).** `dotx service install` unloads the job that is loaded first and writes the new job's property
list once launchd has let the job go (`launchd.install_job`). When the new job does not load, or its file cannot be
written, the file of before is put back, or the new one removed when there was none, and the job of before, when it was
loaded, is loaded again; the install fails with launchd's words, and when the job of before does not load either, the
error names both failures. Before, the new file was written first: a job that could not be unloaded ran beside a file it
was not loaded from, and a new job that did not load left its file and no job. Tests: `tests/unit/test_launchd.py`
installs jobs through a stand-in for `launchctl`, so the job of this Mac is left alone: a job launchd refuses leaves the
job of before and its file, or no file when there was no job (the code of before left the refused file and no job), and
a job launchd cannot unload keeps its file (before: the new file was in its place).

**What.** `dotx service install` takes the running job down before it writes the new job file, and puts the old file
back when the new job does not load, instead of leaving a new file next to an old job, or no job, after a failed step.

### 188. A run of a dotx command is followed live on the pages and stopped there

**Status: done.** Merged as `5f294aa` (PR #227; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** The daemon relays what the runs of other processes store: every half second it tells its
pages the events that the runs of `dotx` commands stored since, and keeps the runs at work of the commands that live
(`RunManager.relay_elsewhere`; the detail of such a run says `elsewhere`). Such a run works in the sidebar and in
Activity, its questions wait there, and its page follows it live, in one stream, to its end (its text comes whole at
each step: what is streamed as it is written is not stored). A read that the store or the files of the owners refuse
leaves the relay going, and a queue whose move the store refused is moved at the next relay. Its Stop asks the command
to stop it through a row of the store (`run_stops`), which the command reads every half second; the command also takes
from the store a decision made on the pages for a question or an approval of its run, which ends the prompt at its
terminal, and an answer typed there after the pages answered no longer fails the command. A command leaves its chat's
queue to the daemon, which moves it once it sees the run end (`RunManager.leave_queues`). The store refuses a run on a
chat where another process drives a run at work, and on a chat whose queued message another process is starting (the gap
the review of item 184 left); a process keeps its own runs apart itself, as before. A start of the daemon that meets the
run of a command that died closes that run first; a command leaves that to the daemon. Before, the daemon did not know
of a command's run: its page asked again and again, Activity counted nothing at work, its Stop answered that the run was
not active, a decision made on the pages reached the command only at the end of its wait (15 minutes), and a message
queued on its chat stayed in the queue after the run ended. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_command_runs.py` runs `dotx run` in
a child process (`tests/fixtures/dot_cli_steps.py`) beside a served daemon: the run on the pages and its live stream,
its Stop, a question answered on its page and an answer typed at the terminal after that, its chat's queue after its
end, also with the store refusing a read of the relay and the first read of the ended run, the run a dead command left,
and its page in Chrome, wide and on a phone, light and dark; `tests/unit/test_one_run_per_chat.py` refuses the second
run with two stores on one database. Each fails on the code of before.

**What.** A run that a `dotx` command drives is listed as working on the pages, and its page follows it live from the
store instead of reconnecting in a loop; its Stop asks the command to stop it, instead of answering that the run is not
active.

### 189. A message sent twice starts once

**Status: done.** Merged as `d615961` (PR #228; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** The pages send each new message with a key of their own (`static/js/sending.js`): a new chat,
a follow-up, a queued message and a steer. A message keeps its key until it is sent; one that changed (its text, its
files, its choices, where it goes) gets a new key. The daemon keeps the keys for a day (`sent_messages`,
`dotagent.server.sending.send_once`): the same message sent again with its key, after an answer that was lost, is
answered with the run its first sending started or steered, or with the chat's queue, instead of a second chat, run,
queued message or steer. A key whose first sending is under way is refused (409); one under way for two minutes is taken
for a sending its daemon left part way. A sending that failed lets its key go. The keys of a run, a steer and a queued
message are apart, and a message without a key (the API used directly) is done each time, as before. Before, a message
whose answer was lost and that was sent again started a second run in a second chat, or was queued or steered a second
time. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_sent_once.py` sends a new chat, a queued message and a steer twice with one key to a
served daemon, a message whose sending failed and one whose sending is under way, and the page that loses the answer to
its first sending and sends the message again, in Chrome, wide and on a phone, light and dark;
`tests/unit/test_sent_messages.py` takes a key once, again once its sending went stale or failed, and anew once it is
forgotten. Each fails on the code of before.

**What.** The pages send a key with each new message, and a message sent again with the same key (after an answer that
was lost) gets the run or the queued message of the first, instead of a second chat or a second run.

### 190. The pages say what they could not read, follow the rules and tell of an update

**Status: done.** Merged as `8f92f36` (PR #229; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** A chat whose queue could not be read says why in the queue's place, with **Read again**, and
keeps what the queue showed before (`static/js/queue.js`). The rules page reads its rules again when one is added,
switched or deleted on another page: the daemon tells the pages each change as a live event of the lifecycle stream
(`rules_changed`), and the page reads again once the stream is back. The sign-in screen of a daemon that could not
answer says that `dotx service status` names the folder of its log, instead of naming `~/Library/Logs/Dot/dotx.log`,
where the log of a daemon given another folder (`DOT_LOG_DIR`) is not. A page loaded before Dot was updated says so in a
banner, with **Load again**: the status of the daemon tells what the pages it serves are (`pages`, a digest of their
files at its start, `dotagent.server.app.pages_build`), and a page compares it with what it read first; Dot's version
does not change with an update, so it could not tell. Before, a queue that could not be read showed nothing, as if its
messages were gone; the rules page showed a rule changed elsewhere only once loaded again; and a page went on beside an
updated daemon without a word. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_pages_tell.py` serves a daemon to Chrome: a queue whose read the
daemon refuses and that is read again, the sign-in screen of a daemon whose status fails and a page whose daemon tells
of other pages, each wide and on a phone, light and dark, and the rules page beside rules added, switched and deleted
through the API; `tests/unit/test_pages_build.py` follows the bytes and the place of each file. Each fails on the code
of before.

**What.** A chat whose queue could not be read says so, with a way to read it again; the rules page follows the changes
made in another window; the sign-in error names the log by what `dotx daemon` prints, not by a path the logs may not be
in; a page loaded before the daemon was updated says so and offers to load again.

### 191. The desktop shell says what it could not read

**Status: done.** Merged as `a0d5eef` (PR #230; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** When the desktop shell could not read the daemon's files, the menu bar item's tip and the
page the window shows while the daemon is down say which file and why, instead of "Dot is not running": a `config.toml`
that is not valid TOML or not the shape of a config, with the line and column of the fault as the parser names them; a
`config.toml` or token file it may not read, in the system's words; an empty token file; and a home without a token file
yet, which the daemon makes the first time it starts (the page then keeps the advice to start Dot). The shell guesses no
address in place of a `config.toml` it could not read; without the file it keeps the daemon's defaults, as the daemon
does. The page reads what the shell tells it in its fragment (`down_url`, `desktop/ui/down.js`), and the shell sends it
again when that changes. Before, the shell took such a file for a missing one, a config for the defaults and a token for
none, and said that Dot was not running. Tests: the shell's own (`cargo test`) read a home with each of these files, and
the address of the page; `tests/smoke/test_down_page.py` opens the page in Chrome, wide and on a phone, light and dark,
told of a config it could not read, then of a home without a token, then of nothing. The page's test fails on the page
of before; the shell's tests do not build on the code of before, which had nothing to tell.

**What.** The desktop shell says why it cannot reach Dot when it cannot read its own files: a `config.toml` that is not
valid TOML (with its line), a token it may not read, a daemon that has not made its token yet, instead of "Dot is not
running" for all of them.

## Part 31: Office files, previews, visuals and questions (planned 2026-10-14)

The owner's thirtieth word, on 2026-10-14: Dot should master Excel, Word and OneDrive, which matter a great deal to the
owner; the Excel, Word and PDF files sent to a chat, or picked from the side menu, should open in a panel beside it; the
chat should show charts, 3D drawings and other visuals, as T3 Code has begun to; and the agent should ask questions in
the middle of its work, with its recommendation, and take a typed answer. Research carefully, and build it the cleanest
way.

**Status (2026-10-14): planned.** What exists was read in the code. `ask_user` offers options as words alone
(`tools/meta.py`); attachments take images, PDF and text and refuse Word, Excel and PowerPoint files
(`agent/attachments.py`), and the page shows only the images among them; nothing of Dot's own making is shown as a page,
and the pages' policy frames nothing (`server/guard.py`); Dot drives applications with AppleScript and the accessibility
tools, with nothing of its own about Office. T3 Code's pages (`html_render`) were read for the frame: a page kept as a
file, served in a sandbox without its origin, sized by a message from inside it and given the theme's colours.
Microsoft's own MCP servers for Word and OneDrive need a work or school account (Microsoft Entra); Excel and Word for
Mac still take AppleScript, which macOS asks the owner to allow once.

**The shape of this part (the decisions).** Five items, each a pull request of its own: a question offers its options
with what each leads to and the one recommended (192); the chat shows pages Dot makes (193); Dot reads Word, Excel and
PowerPoint files (194); a file opens in a panel beside the chat (195); Dot knows its way around Word, Excel and OneDrive
on the Mac (196). Two answers of the owner shape item 196 (open owner decisions 37 and 38): whether Excel and the
OneDrive app are installed, and whether the Microsoft account is personal or of work or school.

### How to start part 31 (the handoff prompt)

> Read ROADMAP.md part 31 and the status table of part 9 (rows 192 to 196). One item at a time, in order; the protocol
> of part 5 (branch, gate, PR, Linear MYP issue when the connector is signed in, squash merge, hash in the table, log
> line) is unchanged. Give each change a test that fails on the code of before, and check a page that changes in a
> browser, wide and on a phone, light and dark. A page Dot makes runs in a frame that cannot reach the daemon or the
> page around it. Never touch the owner's data directory except to read it, by the kinds and numbers of what is
> stored, and to restart the daemon when `/api/status` shows no active run; PLAN.md stays untracked. The owner reads
> Turkish; everything written is English.

### 192. A question offers its options with what each leads to and the one recommended

**Status: done.** Merged as `5a41ac7` (PR #232; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** `ask_user` offers its options with what each leads to (`description`) and the one the run
recommends (`recommended`), and lets several be chosen (`multiple`); options given as words alone, as before, are
options without a description (`dotagent.agent.questions`). The answer stays one text: the labels chosen, joined, then
what the user wrote on a line of its own. The card shows a row for each option, its label over what it leads to and the
one recommended marked: a row sends its option, and when several may be chosen they are ticked and sent with Send
answer, which sends nothing while nothing is ticked or written. The terminal numbers the options, and a number typed
(several, separated by commas) stands for its option. The run reads which option was chosen alone, and whether it was
the one it recommended; the system prompt asks for options and a recommendation when the agent asks. The core tools'
share of the task tools' schemas grows from 0.449 to 0.454 for it (the bound of `tests/unit/test_tool_groups.py` moves
from 0.45 to 0.46). Before, options were words on small buttons, without what each leads to or a recommendation, and
only one could be chosen. Tests: `tests/unit/test_questions.py` (the options as given and as stored, the answer, a typed
number, what the run reads) and `tests/smoke/test_question_choices.py`, a daemon's pages in Chrome, wide and on a phone,
light and dark: a row sends the recommended option, and several ticked are sent with what was written, after a Send
answer with nothing that sent nothing. On the code of before the run could not ask that question at all: `ask_user`
refused described options.

**What.** A question of the agent offers its options with what each leads to and the one it recommends, lets several be
chosen when that fits, and always takes an answer of the user's own words.

### 193. The chat shows pages Dot makes: charts, 3D drawings and other visuals

**Status: done.** Merged as `1cc6fac` (PR #233; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** `show_page(title, html)` keeps a page the run writes in HTML (up to 500,000 characters) in
the database under an id that cannot be guessed, and the run's `page_shown` event names it; the chat shows it in a card
under its title, with Open, which shows it full size in the browser. The daemon serves the page at `/pages/<id>` without
the token, not signed with it as planned: the id is the page's key, so an address that opens in the browser carries
nothing made from the token. It serves the page after a bootstrap of its own and with a policy of its own
(`PAGE_HEADERS` of `server/guard.py`): sandboxed to its scripts, framed or full size, so its origin is opaque, it reads
nothing of the web UI and it reaches neither the API nor the page around it; it fetches nothing but libraries from four
CDNs (cdn.jsdelivr.net, unpkg.com, cdnjs.cloudflare.com, esm.sh), submits no form, and only the pages of the daemon
frame it, which may now frame pages of their own server (`frame-src 'self'`). The frame and the page speak three
messages of the MCP Apps protocol, as T3 Code's pages do: the page tells its height (80 to 2,000 pixels), the frame
sends the colours of the theme on screen as CSS variables and sends them again when the theme or the system's scheme
changes, and a link the user clicks in the page opens in the browser. A script of the page cannot open one by itself,
nor with a click made elsewhere: the frame must hold the focus as well as the click. A page that loads another page in
its frame (a script or a refresh of its own) is closed, with Show it again. A page goes with its chat and with the
events of its run (`dotx prune`), the service worker never caches one, and `dotx run` prints a page's address. The tool
is in a group of its own, `pages`, and the system prompt asks for a page when a chart, a table, a diagram or a 3D view
would say more than words. The tool adds about 420 estimated tokens to the fixed part of the prompt, so the small window
of `tests/smoke/test_scaffold.py` grows from 26,000 to 27,000 tokens, as item 34 grew it, to leave room for two pages
after every compaction. Before, a run showed nothing but text and the screenshots of its tools. Tests:
`tests/unit/test_pages.py` (the document served, its headers and the UI's, how long a page is kept) and
`tests/smoke/test_shown_pages.py`, a daemon's pages in Chrome, wide and on a phone, light and dark: the page sits in its
card in the theme on screen and as tall as it is, and takes the other scheme's colours; its scripts reach neither the
API nor the page around it nor the UI's storage, framed or full size; a link clicked in it opens, and one it asked for
by itself does not; once it loads another page in its frame, the card closes it and shows it again on request. The same
test passed in WebKit, the engine of the desktop shell. With the pages of before the card never shows, and without
`frame-src 'self'` the frame never loads.

**What.** A tool keeps a page of HTML the run writes (a chart, a 3D drawing, a table, a diagram), and the chat shows it
in a card, as T3 Code shows the pages its agents render. The daemon serves the page at an address of its own, signed
with the token, in a frame that gives it no way to the daemon or to the page around it (a sandbox without the same
origin) and no network but scripts and styles from a few package CDNs; the card sizes the frame to the page and hands it
the colours of the theme in use.

### 194. Dot reads Word, Excel and PowerPoint files

**Status: done.** Merged as `5592965` (PR #234; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** Word, Excel and PowerPoint files of Office Open XML (`.docx`; `.xlsx` and `.xlsm`; `.pptx`)
can be attached, as the `office` kind, and their text reaches the model in the message as a PDF's does
(`dotagent.office`, with `python-docx`, `openpyxl` and `python-pptx`). A document reads as its paragraphs and tables in
order, headings and list items marked as Markdown marks them, and a table as a Markdown table; a workbook reads sheet by
sheet (its name, and hidden when it is), a line for each row that holds anything, each cell after its address and a
formula with the value Excel last worked out for it, or not worked out yet when no program that calculates saved it; at
most 100,000 cells, and the text says where it stops. Every sheet is read to its last cell: a sheet read only stops
where the size it records of itself ends, and a file another program wrote can record one too small. A presentation
reads slide by slide, its title first, then the text of its shapes (those in groups too, a paragraph indented by its
level), its tables, its charts (title, kind, and each series' values by category; a chart of a kind `python-pptx` does
not read, 3D bars or a stock chart, is named as not read, and the rest of the slide is read) and its notes. `read_file`
reads such a file on disk the same way, paged by its lines like a PDF. A file of before 2007 (`.doc`, `.xls`, `.ppt`) or
one locked with a password is refused, at upload and by `read_file`, saying what to save instead, and a broken one says
that it cannot be read and why. Before, attachments refused Word, Excel and PowerPoint files, and `read_file` called
them binary. Tests: `tests/unit/test_office.py` (files made with the same libraries, two of them edited in their zip
packages into what the libraries do not write) and the attachment test of `tests/smoke/test_server.py`, which uploads a
Word document, a workbook and a presentation and finds their text in the message the model reads, and is refused a
workbook of before 2007 and a locked document.

**What.** A Word, Excel or PowerPoint file attached to a chat reaches the model as text: a document's paragraphs and
tables, a sheet's cells with their addresses and formulas, a presentation's slides and notes. A tool reads such a file
on disk the same way, a part at a time (`openpyxl`, `python-docx`, `python-pptx`). Before, attachments refused them.

### 195. A file opens in a panel beside the chat: PDF, sheets, documents and more

**Status: done.** Merged as `6ef8fa8` (PR #235; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** A file opens in the side panel of the run page, which the file takes while it is open: half
of the page when the panel has its own width, the whole screen on a phone; Close and Escape give the panel back as it
was and the focus to what opened the file. It opens from a sent file's chip, from a file's path an answer names in code
(`~/...` or `/Users/<name>/...`, to a name with a suffix; the prompt asks the model to name a file by its full path, in
backticks), from the panel's Files card, which lists the conversation's files (those its messages carried and those its
answers name, as it shows them), and from a file's path in Actions (the files the run changed with its file tools):
these, rather than a list in the side menu, are where a chat's files are. `dotagent.previews` reads the file.
`located_file` finds it, its links followed, in the workspace or in the home folder outside hidden folders and outside
`~/Library`, but for `~/Library/CloudStorage` (OneDrive) and `~/Library/Mobile Documents` (iCloud Drive), and every
route of `server/routes_files.py` finds its file with it; `shown_kind` tells how to show the file by its first bytes. A
PDF shows its pages as PNGs that Core Graphics draws on a worker thread at one of four widths (`GET /api/files/page`) as
they come into view, in their proportions and turned as the page says; a locked PDF says so. A workbook and a CSV or TSV
table (its delimiter sniffed: a comma, or a semicolon where the comma marks decimals; its byte order mark read) show as
a grid of the rows and the columns that hold anything, under their numbers and letters, with a tab for each sheet (a
hidden one named so), at most 20,000 cells; a click on a cell says what it holds, its formula and the value last worked
out, or that it is not worked out yet. A Word document shows its headings, paragraphs, lists and tables, and a
presentation its slides with their text by level, tables, charts' series by category and notes: `dotagent.office` now
reads a file into typed models, and makes the text for the model from them as before. An image is drawn from
`GET /api/files/image`, a text shows as text (at most 512 KB), and any other file says why it is not shown (one of
before 2007 says what to save instead). **Open on the Mac** (`POST /api/files/open`, `open` of Launch Services) opens a
document of a kind in `OPENED_SUFFIXES`, never a script, a page or a program. The prompt's line costs the small-window
scaffold test 14 tokens of its margin (its largest step is 20,232 of 20,250). Tests: `tests/unit/test_previews.py` (the
places shown and refused, a link out of them, the kinds by first bytes, a CSV split at its semicolons and cut, a text
cut between characters, a workbook's formulas, a PDF's pages drawn at a width) and `tests/smoke/test_file_panel.py` in
Chrome at 1280 and 390 px, light and dark: a PDF, a workbook, a document and a presentation from their chips; from their
paths in the answer, a CSV table that opens on the Mac through a stand-in, a text whose markup shows as written, an
image, and a file in a hidden folder refused; the Files card, and the file the run wrote from Actions; the routes refuse
`/etc/hosts` and a script to open, and draw a page as a PNG. It passed in WebKit too. Before, chips and paths were text,
and nothing showed a file.

**What.** A file of the chat opens in a panel beside it: an attachment, or a file a run wrote, from its chip or from a
list of the chat's files in the side menu. A PDF shows as it is, a sheet as a grid, a document as its text with its
headings and tables, an image and plain text as they are; on a phone the panel takes the screen. Open in app opens the
file in its application on the Mac.

### 196. Dot knows its way around Word, Excel and OneDrive on the Mac

**Status: done.** Merged as `6be48a8` (PR #275; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-15).** Three skills come with Dot (`src/dotagent/skills/builtin/`). `excel` says when to change a
workbook with openpyxl and how to get the results of its formulas, which openpyxl does not compute (worked out in
Python, or read from a copy LibreOffice computes without a window), and gives the terms of Excel's dictionary for
driving it. `word` says how to change a document's text with python-docx without losing the formatting of its runs and
where text hides (tables, headers), and gives the terms of Word's dictionary. `onedrive` says where OneDrive keeps its
folders (`~/Library/CloudStorage`), what a file kept only online needs, and that a change there reaches the cloud. They
are read after every other skill, so the owner's own skill of a name is used instead without a problem reported, and
`[skills] builtin = false` leaves them out. They name Dot's own Python as `{{dot_python}}`, which the `skill` tool fills
with its path: the shell's `python3` lacks the libraries, and the shell guard asks about a command whose name only a
variable gives. `dotx doctor` lists Excel, Word and LibreOffice with their versions and counts the OneDrive folders by
the kind of account, never by name, and opens nothing. Two eval tasks check the skills, their easy way the skill that
comes with Dot. `excel-add-a-month` starts from a workbook whose totals hold the results Excel saved: a run that reports
those, saves the workbook as openpyxl read its results or leaves the new month out of a formula fails.
`word-rename-company` starts from a letter whose company name is bold in one place, split over two italic runs in
another, and also in a table and the header. The seeds of an eval task may be bytes, in Base64, and both references pass
without Office. Tests: `tests/unit/test_skills.py` and `tests/unit/test_evals.py`; `tests/smoke/test_evals_runner.py`
replays both references through the real loop, and the skills, help and scaffold smoke tests count the skills that come
with Dot (the small window of the scaffold test is 1,000 tokens wider for the skill tool and its section). On the code
of before, the new tests fail to import. Not tried on this Mac: Excel and Word driven by AppleScript, whose first use
asks the owner to allow it, and LibreOffice's computing: it was never opened here, and macOS asks to confirm its first
start.

**What.** Dot knows the ways to Word, Excel and OneDrive on the Mac. Built-in skills say when to edit a file with the
libraries (and recalculate a workbook through Excel or LibreOffice), when to drive the application with AppleScript, and
where OneDrive keeps the files it syncs (`~/Library/CloudStorage/OneDrive-*`); `dotx doctor` says which of them are
installed, and eval tasks check the skills.

## Part 32: runs that stop whole, every agent in the side menu, a model that stays (planned 2026-10-14)

The owner's thirty-first word, on 2026-10-14: the default model should be chosen in Settings, and the model chosen in a
chat should stay chosen through a reload or a restart; reconnecting should be sure to work; small marks at the left of
the conversation, one for each message, should show the message when the pointer rests on one and go to it on a click,
as in T3 Code; once a run is stopped, the rows of the runs it delegated should stop moving; a run with three agents at
work showed one of them in the side menu, and they could not be folded or unfolded; and the left menu and the right
panel should both be designed and work better, after T3 Code or in a way of Dot's own.

**Status (2026-10-14): planned.** What exists was read in the code. A run that was stopped stored its end before the
ends of the runs it delegated (`RunManager.delegate` stopped a delegated run and went on at once), and the run page
reads a run's events up to its own end: the rows of those runs kept working. So did a crash's: the daemon that starts
next stores the ends it left in the order the runs were made. The side menu's Working section lists the runs at work
alone (`server/activity.py`): a delegated run that ended leaves it, and the rows under a run do not fold. The default
model is `[models] main` in `config.toml`, which Settings shows and no page changes; a chat's composer takes the model
of the run its page shows, and a model picked there and not sent is lost with a reload. The pages follow their streams
again after a break and read again what changed (item 160); the first screen of a daemon that is down waits for a click,
a few pages read nothing again, and the desktop shell polls the daemon every second. The conversation has no marks of
its messages.

**The shape of this part (the decisions).** Seven items, each a pull request of its own, the defects first: a stopped
run stops the runs it delegated, and their rows stop (197); the side menu shows every agent of a run, folded under it
(198); the default model is chosen in Settings, and a chat keeps its model (199); reconnecting is checked end to end,
and what it misses is mended (200); then the marks of the conversation's messages (201), and the side menu (202) and the
run's side panel (203) designed again, in their structure and in how they work. Item 196 of part 31 follows the defects
(197 to 200) unless the owner orders otherwise.

### How to start part 32 (the handoff prompt)

> Read ROADMAP.md part 32 and the status table of part 9 (rows 197 to 203). One item at a time, in order; the protocol
> of part 5 (branch, gate, PR, Linear MYP issue when the connector is signed in, squash merge, hash in the table, log
> line) is unchanged. Give each change a test that fails on the code of before, and check a page that changes in a
> browser, wide and on a phone, light and dark. Never touch the owner's data directory except to read it, by the
> kinds and numbers of what is stored, and to restart the daemon when `/api/status` shows no active run; PLAN.md
> stays untracked. The owner reads Turkish; everything written is English.

### 197. A stopped run stops the runs it delegated, and their rows stop

**Status: done.** Merged as `0b3a7d4` (PR #236; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** A run that is stopped stops the runs it delegated, and its end is stored after theirs.
`RunManager.delegate`, cancelled while it waits, stops the delegated run and lets the cancellation go on once that run's
end is stored; the calls of a turn that run together are all awaited before the turn's cancellation goes on
(`executor._together`), so the run's own end comes last. The run page reads a run's events up to its own end: each row
of a delegated run now ends on the page that watched the stop, and on every page opened after it. A daemon that starts
stores the ends a crash left behind (`Store.mark_interrupted_runs`), and the daemon the ends of the runs of a `dotx`
command that died (`Store.close_runs_of`), those of delegated runs first. A run stored the other way, before this item,
shows its rows ended too: once its own end is read, the page reads the run again, as it did, and a row whose run has
ended shows how, from the run's `children` (`timeline.settle`). Before, the rows of a stopped run's delegated runs kept
their ring and their last line ("starting", or their last step), after a reload too. Tests:
`tests/smoke/test_stopped_delegation.py`, a real server on the scripted model, in Chrome at 1280 and 390 px, light and
dark: a run delegates three runs that wait in a shell command, the page's Stop ends them all as stopped with their ends
stored before the run's, and every row shows its run cancelled, on that page and after a reload; a run stored the old
way shows its row cancelled. `tests/unit/test_store_runs.py`: both ways of closing what a process left store the
delegated run's end first. On the code of before, a delegated run was still at work once the run that delegated it had
ended (`('running', '') == ('cancelled', ...)`), the row of the old way kept working, and a restart stored the run's end
first (`2 < 1`). It passed in WebKit too.

### 198. The side menu shows every agent of a run, folded under it

**Status: done.** Merged as `dee248f` (PR #237; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** Under a run at work, the side menu's Working section shows every run it delegated: those at
work with Working and their time, as before, and those that ended with how they ended (their face or dot at rest, the
status first in their facts). `GET /activity` lists the ended ones apart, as `ended_delegated` (the runs that the runs
at work delegated and that have ended; Ended today leaves them out until their run ends), so that the sections, the
home's line and its Today strip count what works as before; the side menu and Activity hang them under their run. A line
under the run says how many runs it delegated and, while some have ended, how many of them work ("3 delegated runs · 1
working"); a click on it folds them, in place, so the focus stays on it, and the fold is kept with the folds of the
sections (`dot.sideFolds`, the runs folded, forgotten once their run is no longer listed). Before, the section listed
the delegated runs at work alone, the line under the run said "1 delegated run" while three were, and nothing folded
them. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_side_agents.py`, a real server on the scripted model, in Chrome at 1280 and 390 px, light
and dark: a run delegates three runs, two of which finish while the third waits in a shell command; the section counts
two at work, the line says "3 delegated runs · 1 working", the three rows show under it, two of them done, and a fold is
kept after a reload; the Activity page shows the three under the run and counts two. On the code of before, the section
showed one row under the run and no line to fold them. It passed in WebKit too.

**What.** The Working section lists, under a run at work, every run it delegated: those at work with how long they have
worked, those that ended with how they ended. The run's row folds them, and keeps the fold.

### 199. The default model is chosen in Settings, and a chat keeps its model

**Status: done.** Merged as `de8069e` (PR #238; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** Settings › Models opens with **Default model**, a menu of the models that can call tools (as
the composer offers them) and of the default one, listed or not. A pick is `POST /api/models/main`: the provider is
asked about the model (one it does not know fails with its error, one that cannot call tools is refused with 422),
`config.toml` gets `[models] main` with its comments and its other settings as they were (`config_edit.set_setting`, for
a `[models]` setting as for a `[browser]` one; a file it cannot change is refused, with how to change it by hand), and
only then the daemon starts the runs that name no model on it, at once: a new chat's, a schedule's, an agent's without a
model of its own. `/api/status` and the health checks say the default as it is now, so the composer's Default and the
badge of the Models table follow it. A chat keeps its choices (`ChatChoices`: the mode, the model, the reasoning level,
the approvals and goal mode) in the `threads` table: those its first run started with (a chat from before: those of its
next run), then each one picked in its composer, sent to `PATCH /api/threads/{id}` at once and one after the other, so
that the last one made is kept. `GET /api/runs/{id}` has them as `choices`, and the chat's page starts its composer from
them; a run moved to a standby model leaves them as they are, so a follow-up starts on the chat's model again. Before,
the composer started from the open run: a reload lost what was picked, and after a move to a standby model it showed
that model. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_chat_choices.py`, a real server on scripted models, in Chrome at 1280 and 390 px,
light and dark: the default picked in Settings starts a run that names no model, the home's composer and the file have
it, and a model without tools is refused; a chat's mode, model, level and approvals picked in its composer are there
after a reload and in another browser, and its follow-up starts with them; a run moved to a standby model leaves the
chat's model. Unit tests for `[models] main` in the file and for the store. On the code of before, Settings had no such
menu, a reload showed Task again, and the composer showed the standby model. It passed in WebKit too.

**What.** Settings chooses the model new chats start on (`[models] main`), with no edit of `config.toml` by hand and no
restart of the daemon. A chat keeps the model and the reasoning chosen in it, through a reload of the page and a restart
of the app or of the daemon.

### 200. Reconnecting, checked end to end

**Status: done.** Merged as `0dab7de` (PR #239; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** Every way a page loses the daemon was tried against a real server, stopped and started again
at its address. A page open while the daemon restarts came back by itself already (item 160) and still does: it says
that it reconnects, is live again once the daemon is back and reads what changed, without loading again. Three ways did
not. A page loaded while the daemon is down, from the service worker's copy of the shell as a phone has it, said that
the daemon ran but could not answer (an error without a status, which nothing that is the daemon answered, was taken for
the daemon's answer) and waited for a click; it now says that it cannot reach the daemon and tries again by itself,
after 2 seconds, then twice as long each time up to 30, and at once when the browser is back on the network or the page
back in view, saying when, with **Try again** kept. A stream that stopped without closing, as a network that changed or
a Mac that slept leaves one, stayed silent and the page took it for live; the daemon writes a keepalive into every
stream every 15 seconds, and a stream from which nothing came for 45 is now cut and made again from its last event,
after which the page reads what changed. The pause between tries, half a second growing to 8, started from the shortest
again only once an event came; it now does once a stream is made, and a page back in view or a browser back on the
network tries at once. The desktop window left the UI for its down page after three polls without an answer, so a
restart of the daemon (one to six seconds) loaded the page again; it now waits for ten, and the open page reconnects by
itself. The memory and skills pages read once and follow no stream, and they hold open editors that a read would wipe:
they are left as they were. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_reconnect.py`, a real server in Chrome: a restart with a page open;
a page loaded from the service worker's copy while the daemon is down, at 1280 px light and 390 px dark; a page back in
view and a browser back on the network, each in the middle of its longest pause; a stream through a proxy that stops
passing its bytes without closing them. On the code of before, the page loaded while the daemon was down said that it
ran and waited, the page back in view waited for its pause to end, and the silent stream was never cut; the restart
passed there too. A Rust test for the desktop window fails with three polls. It passed in WebKit too, where a font the
page had not used before the daemon went down, which no copy holds, is told as an error of the page; the page shows the
system's own.

**What.** Every way a page loses the daemon is tried and comes back by itself: a restart of the daemon, a stream that
drops, the app opened while the daemon is down, the Mac waking from sleep. A page that reads nothing again after a break
reads what changed. A test for each.

### 201. Marks of the conversation's messages: a look and a jump, after T3 Code

**Status: done.** Merged as `4f23e25` (PR #240; no Linear issue, the Linear connector was signed out).

**As built (2026-10-14).** At the left of the conversation a column of short marks stands for the owner's messages, one
mark for each, top to bottom as they stand in it (`outline.js`, after T3 Code's): the question of each earlier turn, the
run's goal and each message sent while it worked; a delegated run's are its own. Resting the pointer on the column shows
the message of the mark nearest to it and the start of its answer, the last that Dot wrote before the next message, in
three lines; a click brings that message to the top of what the window shows, under the stage bar. The column is one
button: from the keyboard the arrows, Home and End walk the marks, Enter goes, and the button names the message it goes
to. A mark is short at rest and longer the nearer it is to the one chosen, and the marks of the messages in sight are
darker as the conversation scrolls. The column stands at the left edge of the run's layout, in the middle of what the
window shows between the stage bar and the dock, 8 px between marks until it is as tall as the window lets it be. It
needs a pointer that rests, two messages or more, and 40 px of room at the left of the conversation (its inset, a whole
mark and a little air): a phone has none, and beside the side panel a window needs 1512 px. T3 Code asks for 48, which
the side panel never leaves. Tests: `tests/smoke/test_outline.py`, a real server on a scripted model, with a chat of
five messages and long answers and one of a single message: the marks at 1280 px, light and dark, clear of the
conversation, the one in sight darker; resting on the second shows its message and the start of its answer; a click, and
Enter after the arrows, bring a message into view; no column on a phone, for a single message, or beside the side panel
at 1280 px, and one at 1512 px. On the code of before there was no column. It passed in WebKit too.

**What.** A column of short marks at the left of the conversation, one for each message of the owner: resting on one
shows the message and the start of its answer, and a click goes to it. After T3 Code's.
